items.title: James Chirillo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: you listen to those Basie records for instance

ctx.x: Oh yeah, to answer your question, pardon me, I’m sort of throwing a ball around, running with the ball, I mean there are certain things you’re not — nobody is going to learn at a college because you’re not in a professional playing situation. I mean if you show up to various jobs without, say if you’re a horn player, and you don’t bring your mutes or

something, and the band leader, you know “bring the mutes” aww you don’t feel like bringing them, whatever it is. Sometimes in college guys out there don’t feel like bringing mutes, schlepping them around all day or whatever, so they don’t bring them to class or to the ensemble or whatever, that’s reason enough for the guy not to call you back for the job next time, no matter how good you read. So it’s those kind of things you’re not going to learn at the school. But in terms of all the — we were sight reading…

What a great process of discovery, really, to figure that out. I was zooming around on the internet actually and went looking for you, and I found this response you had written to someone about Freddie Green.
